    Every page, every flow, and what happens in between

    The site has four audiences, three ways in, two sides of a matching engine and one badge that ties them together. This is all of it, drawn — one diagram per flow, each with the files it lives in underneath.

    00

    How to read this

    Seven pages, nineteen sections, one diagram per flow. Each diagram is followed by the files it lives in, so a picture can be traced to the code that makes it true. Colour means the same thing throughout.

    Fair track — students, parents, visitors Conference track — government and officials Exhibitors — universities and institutes Operations — staff, gate, scheduled jobs
    Reading a diagram

    A rounded box is a person. A rectangle is a page or a step. A diamond is a decision. A cylinder is something written to the database. Wide diagrams scroll sideways inside their own frame — the page itself never does.

    01

    The whole thing at a glance

    Four kinds of people use this, and each has their own front door and their own login. They never see each other's screens, but everything they do lands in the same three places: the registration record, the shared taxonomy of subjects, and the message log.

    In the code
    • routes/site.phpEverything under a language prefix
    • routes/web.phpTickets, check-in, webhooks, QR
    • config/auth.phpThe three separate logins
    02

    URLs and language

    Every readable page lives under a language segment — /en/agenda, /ku/agenda, /ar/agenda — so a link can be shared without losing the language it was read in. English is what a first-time visitor gets; after that the choice is remembered for a year.

    In the code
    • app/Http/Middleware/SetLocale.phpResolves and remembers the language
    • app/Http/Controllers/LocaleController.phpSwitcher and the redirect fallback
    • lang/en · lang/ku · lang/arEvery string, three times
    03

    Three doors, one badge

    Someone who wants to walk in should not have to fill in four steps, and a government delegate should not be sent a WhatsApp code. So there are four doors — but they all end at the same thing: one row in registrations, one ticket reference, one QR that the gate can scan.

    Only one of them opens an account. A student is registering and creating a Next Step ID in the same form, because everything else Next Step runs — the agenda, the seminars, Zankoline, the scholarship — reads that one record. A parent, a visitor and a delegate get a badge and are left alone.

    DoorAsks forProves identity byBadge arrivesGets an account
    Visitor passName, phoneWhatsApp codeWhatsApp imageNo
    ParentName, phone, cityWhatsApp codeWhatsApp imageNo
    StudentOne short form, plus email and passwordWhatsApp codeWhatsApp imageYes — the Next Step ID
    ConferenceSeven fieldsEmail domainEmail PDF + ICSNo
    04

    Expo registration

    One page each. A student answers seven things and sets a password, because they are creating the account the rest of the programme runs on. A parent answers three and gets a badge.

    Gone from both: gender, stream, subject chips, why you are coming, which days, where you heard about us, and which seminars — asked later in the place they matter, or not worth asking. Every badge is valid for all three days, so nobody picks days at all. Nothing is written to the database until the form is submitted, and no badge exists until the phone number answers.

    In the code
    • app/Http/Controllers/Registration/FairRegistrationController.phpThe whole flow
    • app/Http/Requests/StoreFairRegistrationRequest.phpServer-side rules
    • app/Services/Messaging/OtpService.phpCodes, expiry, resend cooldown
    • app/Services/BadgeService.phpBadge artwork
    05

    Completing a visitor pass

    Someone who took the quick route can come back and finish. The point of the flow is that nothing is asked twice: the pass already carries a name and a phone number that answered a code, so the form starts from what is known and the badge never changes.

    Why it matters

    A visitor pass that becomes a full registration keeps its place in every count that has already been taken — no duplicate row, no second badge at the gate, and any check-in already recorded still belongs to the same person.

    06

    One number, one badge

    Both fair forms check the phone number against the list before creating anything. A number that is already registered gets told so, on the page it was typed on, with a way forward rather than a dead end.

    07

    Conference RSVP

    The conference is a one-day event for ministries, embassies, agencies, press, companies and individuals. It is not a phone-and-QR flow: delegates are confirmed by their institutional email address, and the badge arrives as an A6 PDF with a calendar invite attached.

    Seven fields and a tick box. Dietary requirements, interpretation, delegation size, invitation letters, speaking slots and press accreditation are all conversations to have with the handful of delegates they concern, not a wall of questions in front of everybody else.

    In the code
    • app/Http/Controllers/Registration/ConferenceRsvpController.phpOne form, review split
    • app/Mail/RsvpConfirmation.phpEmail with PDF and ICS
    • app/Http/Controllers/TicketController.phpManage and cancel by signed link
    08

    The Next Step ID

    Students get an account; nobody else does. A scholarship application runs for months and has to be reachable from a school computer or a sibling's laptop, so a student signs in with the email and password they set when they registered.

    A parent, a visitor or a delegate has nothing to sign into. If they lose the WhatsApp message they ask for the badge again by phone number and a code — the same check that issued it. That is also what connects the agenda to registration: a guest who presses add to my agenda does not lose the click.

    What /me holds

    PageShowsVisitor pass sees it?

    /me/agendaThe full programme, add and removeNo — offered the upgrade
    /me/interestsOptional. Eight questions, offered from the account and never during registrationNo
    /me/matchesRanked universities with the reason for each scoreNo
    /me/editTheir own details, and a photo. Everything the short form left out, at their own paceYes

    09

    What registering is worth

    A registration form is a cost paid up front against a promise. The board under /{lang}/opportunities is where that promise is paid back: scholarships the ministry has opened, a tuition reduction a university negotiated with Next Step, a free summer school, a place on a programme. They are put there by partners and they are only shown to somebody who has a badge.

    That is also why the home page is not the same page twice. Signed out, it sells the fair and its one large button says register. Signed in, that button is already spent — the hero greets the person by name and by ticket, and the space the registration pitch used to hold now carries their agenda, the scholarship, the opportunities, Zankoline, the exhibitor list and the seminars.

    Who is shown what

    AudienceReachesUsed for
    everyoneAnyone with a badgeSponsor programmes, open days, prize draws
    studentsStudent accountsTuition reductions, summer schools, competitions
    grade12Grade 12 and recent leaversScholarships and admissions, where anyone else would be applying to something they cannot take
    parentsParents registered for the expoFinancing talks, parent evenings

    A countdown is only printed inside the last fortnight. On something six months away it is noise; on something closing next week it is the reason to read on. Reads and follows are counted separately — how many opened the record, and how many went on to the partner's own form. The second is what a partner is owed at the end of the season; one column for both would flatter every placement.

    Telling people you are coming

    Most people who find this fair hear about it from somebody they know, so the moment a registration is confirmed the confirmation page asks for a post — and hands over both halves of it. A picture at the size the platform wants (1080×1080 for a feed, 1080×1920 for a story) and a caption already written in the first person, for that particular person: a grade 12 student is choosing a life, a parent is helping somebody else choose one, a director general is representing an institution. One line for all three would be posted by none of them.

    ChannelHow
    WhatsAppOpens with the caption already in it — the channel that matters most here
    Facebook · LinkedInShare dialog with the tagged link
    Instagram feed and storyNo web composer exists. The page says so and offers the picture to save

    Nothing offered for sharing carries the badge QR. That code is the entry credential: on a public feed it is a free pass for whoever screenshots it first. The cards carry the event, the dates and the partnership marks, and nothing that identifies one person.

    The link in the post is /{lang}/attending/{who}, not the home page. It carries the Open Graph tags LinkedIn and Facebook read, pointing at a 1200×630 render of the same card, so the post shows a real preview rather than a logo on a white square — and somebody who clicked because a friend is going lands on a page about that, with a register button on it. None of this needs an account on either platform, an app, or a key: a share button is a plain link and the preview is read off the page.

    The person's name is drawn onto the card in their own browser, on a canvas, and never written to disk. There are as many names as there are people, and a Kurdish or Arabic one needs shaping and bidi that a browser does correctly and PHP's image libraries do not. If the script does not run, the download falls back to the plain card. The slot geometry lives in ShareKit::nameSlot() and is read by both the page and the script, so the two cannot drift apart.

    The twenty-seven cards — three languages, three audiences, three shapes — are pre-rendered PNGs under public/assets/share, screenshots of a real page at /{lang}/share/card/{variant}/{format} taken by tools/build-share-cards.cjs. Rendering them at build time rather than on the server settles the hard part for good: Kurdish and Arabic need contextual shaping and bidi, which a browser does correctly and PHP's image libraries do not.

    In the code
    • app/Services/ShareKit.phpWhich words, which card, which buttons
    • resources/views/components/ns/share-block.blade.phpThe block on both confirmation pages and /me/share
    • tools/build-share-cards.cjsRenders the eighteen cards

    10

    The National Scholarship Program

    Forty fully funded first degrees, held in regional quotas: eight seats for each of the four provinces, two for each of the four independent administrations. A student from Halabja competes against Halabja, not against Sulaymaniyah — which is the whole point, because a single national ranking would send almost every seat to the largest cities.

    It has its own pages under /{lang}/scholarship and its own place in the main menu, but it is not a separate website: it reads the same Next Step ID, so a student who registered for the expo applies without signing up twice.

    What is published before anyone applies

    The quota per region, the participating universities and the departments they have pledged seats to, the scoring weights, the four documents, the dates, and the committee by name. An applicant should be able to see what is judged and what it is worth before writing a word.

    Scored onWeightMeaning
    Academic background40%Exam average, stream and consistency across the years
    Project feasibility35%Whether the proposal could actually start here, with what exists
    Interview25%Clarity, motivation, commitment to come back and work

    Screening comes first and is pass or fail: without the four documents and an average of 85%, a file is closed before any committee member reads it.

    In the code
    • config/scholarship.phpSeats, regions, questions, rubric, universities, dates
    • app/Http/Controllers/Scholarship/ScholarshipController.phpThe public pages
    • app/Http/Controllers/Scholarship/ApplicationController.phpGate, check, form, status
    • app/Models/ScholarshipApplication.phpVerdict, completeness, the stage queue
    11

    Interests and matching

    Both sides describe themselves in one shared vocabulary — 12 sectors, 72 subjects, in all three languages. That is what makes a student's answers and a university's programmes comparable at all, and it is why demand and supply can be counted against each other later.

    What is recomputed, and when

    Matches are not a nightly batch. Saving interests recomputes that student's matches; saving programmes in the portal recomputes that university's. Changing your mind deletes the recommendations that no longer apply, so the list is never stale.

    In the code
    • config/taxonomy.phpSectors, subjects, weights, threshold
    • app/Services/Matching/MatchEngine.phpScoring, both directions
    • app/Http/Controllers/Attendee/InterestsController.phpThe eight questions
    12

    The exhibitor portal

    Universities register themselves. A recruiter claims an institution — or creates one that Next Step then approves — signs in with a code sent to their email, and from there maintains the profile that the public directory shows and the matching engine reads.

    13

    Booth scans, leads and what they answer

    The scanner at a stand is the moment the data becomes real: a badge scanned is a student who physically walked over. Every scan, shortlist and enquiry is stored as an interaction with a weight, which is what separates genuine interest from a page view when the reports are written.

    The questionAnswered fromWhere to look
    Which fields attract the most interest?Stated subjects, weighted by preference order/admin/insights
    Which countries and universities are most popular?Country preferences, profile views, shortlists/admin/insights
    Which universities generated the most qualified leads?Interactions by weight, per organisation/admin/insights
    What does nobody teach that everybody wants?Demand minus supply, per subject/admin/insights
    Did a match turn into a visit?Stored matches against booth scans/admin/insights
    14

    Gate check-in

    The scanner is a small web app that staff open on a phone. It is built to keep working when the hall's wifi does not: it holds the day's expected badges, records arrivals locally, and syncs when the connection returns.

    In the code
    • app/Http/Controllers/Checkin/CheckinController.phpScan, search, manual, offline sync
    • app/Services/TicketService.phpSigning and resolving a ticket
    15

    Messaging

    Nothing is sent while someone waits. Every message is written to the log first and queued second, so a registrant sees their confirmation page immediately and a failed send can be retried from the dashboard instead of being lost.

    Every message the system can send

    TemplateChannelSent when
    otpWhatsAppRegistration or sign-in — 6 digits, 10 minutes, 5 tries
    registration_confirmed_studentWhatsAppStudent verifies, with the badge attached
    registration_confirmed_parentWhatsAppParent verifies, with the badge attached
    registration_confirmed_visitorWhatsAppVisitor pass issued, with the badge attached
    event_reminder_3daysWhatsAppThree days before opening
    event_reminder_1dayWhatsAppThe day before
    day_of_directionsWhatsAppMorning of each day they chose
    session_reminderWhatsApp15 minutes before a saved session
    post_event_thankyou_surveyWhatsAppAfter the fair closes
    rsvp_confirmed · rsvp_pendingEmailConference RSVP, with or without the badge
    reminder_3days · reminder_1dayEmailDelegate reminders
    badge_resent · thankyouEmailOn request, and after the event

    Each row exists three times, once per language, and the wording is the same text submitted to Meta for template approval.

    16

    Campaign QR codes

    Separate from badges: these are the codes printed on posters, banners and school handouts. Each is a short link that counts scans before forwarding, so it is possible to say which poster actually worked.

    17

    The dashboard

    One section per area, grouped by what the person doing the work is thinking about. Roles decide what is visible: gate staff cannot open registrations, and a content editor cannot read personal details.

    18

    Data model

    The registration is the hub. Everything a person does — sessions saved, days attended, messages received, universities matched and met — hangs off that one row, which is why a visitor pass can become a full registration without anything being orphaned.

    What is protected, and how

    DataAt restStill searchable because
    Phone numbersEncryptedA keyed hash column sits beside it
    Email addressesEncryptedSame
    QR contentsTicket id plus signature onlyNothing personal is in the code at all
    Press ID uploadsPrivate disk, never publicReached only from the dashboard
    19

    What runs when

    Reminders are scheduled commands, not something anyone has to remember to press. Each one skips anybody who has already had that message, so running it twice cannot double-send.

    CommandDoes
    nextstep:reminders three-days|one-day|day-ofQueues that reminder wave, skipping anyone already sent it
    nextstep:session-reminders15-minute nudges for bookmarked sessions
    nextstep:badges:regenerateRe-renders badge artwork after a design or key change
    nextstep:qr-secretCreates or rotates the QR signing secret
    nextstep:sitemapRebuilds the sitemap across all three languages
    20

    Guards and limits

    Three separate logins that cannot be swapped for one another: an attendee session does not open the portal, and a portal session does not open the dashboard.

    LoginWhoProves it byReaches
    webNext Step staffEmail and password, roles/admin, /checkin
    attendeeAnyone with a badgePhone plus WhatsApp code/me and everything under it
    institutionUniversity recruitersEmail plus code/portal

    Rate limits

    ActionLimitCounted per
    Submitting a registration6 / minute, 40 / dayIP address
    Entering or resending a code5 / minuteIP address, and per ticket
    Requesting a sign-in code5 / minute, 15 / hourIP, and 3 / minute per phone number
    Lead capture forms4 / minuteIP address
    Gate scanning120 / minuteSigned-in staff member

    Every public form also carries a hidden field a real person never fills in, and a signed session token — so the ordinary bot traffic never reaches the database at all.
